title: The Orison Table
subtitle: Receipts of the House, gathered for the Tenants' Association
foreword: Every flat in this house cooks on a coal range and keeps its milk on ice, and every flat has a signal point beside the stove that can play the Kitchen Hour louder than the kettle. These are the dishes the house actually eats, set down as each tenant gave them to me, with my corrections in red where a correction was owed. Everything here can be had from the bodega or the Arcade. Wash up as you go.

dishes.name: Saturday Beans and Red-Pencil Brown Bread
dishes.origin: New England, by way of a Boston normal school
method: Soak the beans overnight. Parboil until the skins split when you blow on a spoonful.
Lay the onion in the pot, then the beans, then the scored salt pork on top. Stir molasses and mustard into hot water and pour it over to cover.
Bake slow in the range oven all afternoon, topping up the water.
For the bread: stir the three meals with the soda, add buttermilk and the rest of the molasses, fill a greased tin two-thirds and steam it, lidded, in a kettle of water.
Turn the bread out and cut it with a string, never a knife.
dishes.twist: The WORS Kitchen Hour broadcast this receipt in 1925 with a wrong steaming time. Evelyn times her bread instead by the kettle's note: when the pitch drops a third, the bread is done.
dishes.note: She corrects the broadcast every Saturday, aloud, to an empty kitchen. A second plate is always set.
dishes.red_pencil: Three hours, not two. The Kitchen Hour has been told.

dishes.name: Night-Shift Caldo Verde
dishes.origin: Minho, Portugal, by way of the Fall River mills
method: Boil the potatoes with the onion and garlic until they fall apart, then mash them into their own water.
Roll the kale leaves tight and cut them as thin as thread.
Fry the sausage in its own fat with a spoon of oil.
Drop the kale into the soup for three minutes only, so it stays green.
Float the sausage on top, oil over all, and pour it straight into the thermos.
dishes.twist: Teresa slices the kale to the rhythm of the ward's alarm board, recorded on a cylinder she keeps by the range. She says it keeps her hand steady. It also keeps her listening.
dishes.note: Made at 21:00 for the 03:00 meal on the ward. She has never once eaten it at home, sitting down.
dishes.red_pencil: Sit down to eat this at least once. E.M.

dishes.name: Arroz Doce with the Date in Cinnamon
dishes.origin: Portugal; her mother's receipt, transcribed from a voice cylinder
method: Simmer the rice in a little water with a strip of lemon peel until the water is gone.
Add the milk a cup at a time, stirring, until the rice is soft and the pot is thick.
Take it off the heat. Stir in the sugar, then the beaten yolks, quickly.
Pour it into a shallow dish and let it set.
Write on the top in ground cinnamon: a name, a date, a word.
dishes.twist: In Portugal the cinnamon spells a blessing. Mina's mother left the receipt on a voice cylinder, and Mina transcribed it with the timings in the margin. She writes the date on hers, because a dish nobody wrote down did not happen.
dishes.note: Eaten at the desk at 03:00 over the day's captions. The cylinder has a silence in the middle of it, four seconds long, which she has never annotated.
dishes.red_pencil: The silence is part of the receipt. Leave it in.

dishes.name: Fijones for Whoever Comes
dishes.origin: Salonika, Sephardic; brought to Allen Street in 1911
method: Soak the beans overnight with a pinch of soda and rinse them twice.
Brown the beef in oil, then the onions until they are soft and gold.
Add the tomatoes and the paprika and let them cook down red.
Put in the beans with water to cover by a finger, and simmer slow until the beans are creamy and the meat falls.
Make enough for six. Somebody always knocks.
dishes.twist: Lena learned it beside a Vantry dictaphone in the sewing loft, where the girls recorded receipts for each other on the dinner break. The loft burned. The cylinders, in their tin, did not, and she still has the one with her mother's voice on it.
dishes.note: She cooks for six and eats standing at her own door, handing out bowls. The pot is the only thing in 2B that is ever mended visibly.
dishes.red_pencil: Sit at your own table, Lena.

dishes.name: Bramboráky at Three in the Morning
dishes.origin: Bohemia, by way of the Astoria Sokol hall
method: Grate the raw potatoes and squeeze them hard in a cloth.
Mix in the egg, the flour, the crushed garlic, marjoram and a pinch of caraway.
Get the lard smoking in the iron pan.
Flatten spoonfuls thin and fry them until the edges lace and crackle.
Eat them out of the pan with the window open.
dishes.twist: Juno records the frying. The crackle of a bramborák in hot lard is in three of her pseudonymous broadcasts, credited to nobody, and one of them was taken by someone else.
dishes.note: Her grandmother's name is not on this receipt. Juno asked me to leave it off, so I have.

dishes.name: Cock-a-Leekie with the Prunes Left In
method: Cover the hen with cold water, bring it up slowly and skim it clean.
Add the green of the leeks, the carrots and the bay, and simmer three hours.
Lift out the bird, strip the meat and throw the bones and greens on the compost.
Return the meat with the white of the leeks, the rice and the prunes for the last half hour.
Pepper it hard. The prunes stay in.
dishes.twist: The leeks are grown on the Orison roof from Auggie's seed. Malcolm keeps one cutting that he never eats and never plants. The soup is the only thing he lets go to compost.
dishes.note: Auggie took the prunes out every time. Malcolm leaves them in. He says this is the receipt and that is that.

dishes.name: Mujaddara, Repaired
dishes.origin: Mount Lebanon, by way of Washington Street
method: Slice the onions thin and fry them slowly in the oil until they are brown nearly to black.
Boil the lentils until just tender.
Add the rice, the allspice, half the onions and their oil, with water to cover, and cook it covered until dry.
Rest it ten minutes in a towel.
Pile the rest of the onions on top and eat it with white cheese.
dishes.twist: Bell Bros. on Washington Street, his cousins' shop, sells the lentils, sealed in a tin with the Vantry service plate soldered to the lid. Omar fixed the sealing press in 1919. It still works.
dishes.note: He calls it repaired because the burnt onion was a mistake the first time and became the receipt. He eats it to the static on 1610.
dishes.red_pencil: Make a pot for 5C. She will eat it.

dishes.name: Nikujaga, Take One
dishes.origin: Japan; Maizuru naval kitchens, by way of the Harukiya
method: Cut the potatoes in big pieces and bevel the edges so they do not break.
Fry the beef sliced paper-thin with the ginger until it colours.
Add the onion, carrot and potato, then water just to cover.
Season with the sugar first and the shoyu after, never the other way.
Lid it with a smaller lid resting on the food, and simmer until the potato is tender. Do not stir. Serve it as it comes.
dishes.twist: The Harukiya's cook taught her by playing back a disc of his own cooking, the knife and the simmer and nothing else. She sang over it once and ruined the take. That is the version she makes.
dishes.note: Everything else she does she does nineteen times. This she makes once and eats.

dishes.name: Toad-in-the-Hole, as Printed
dishes.origin: England, from a 1909 receipt card, misprint included
method: Beat the flour, eggs and milk into a batter and let it stand one hour exactly.
Heat the dripping in a tin in the range oven until it smokes.
Brown the sausages in it, then pour the batter round them quickly.
Bake until risen and brown. The card says forty minutes at a moderate oven. He gives it forty.
Serve with mustard and onion gravy if there is time. There is not.
dishes.twist: The card is misprinted: it says one tablespoon of mustard in the batter. Peter has followed the misprint every week since 1909 because it is what the card says, and he has certified the card.
dishes.note: Same day, same card, same tin. The card has never been corrected. He will not let me.
dishes.red_pencil: Mustard on the side, Peter. On the side.

dishes.name: Huevos Haminados for the Bridge
dishes.origin: Sephardic; Lena's way, eaten Cam's way
method: Line the pot with all the onion skins you have saved.
Lay the eggs on them, add the spent coffee grounds and a spoon of oil, and cover with water.
Bring it up, then let it sit on the back of the range all night, barely moving.
By morning the shells are mahogany and the whites are the colour of milky coffee.
Six eggs, six pockets.
dishes.twist: The grounds come free from the Luncheonette's urn after close. Cam hard-wires a cheap Vantry pocket timer to the pot so the night can pass without anyone watching it, which is the only kind of rest Cam will allow the eggs.
dishes.note: Eaten one-handed on the bridge at 03:00. Lena makes them sit down to peel one. It takes eleven minutes.

dishes.name: Cawl on the Daily Set
dishes.origin: Wales; the Price family's, kept as found
method: Simmer the lamb in cold water for an hour, skimming.
Let it cool and lift the fat off the top.
Add the potatoes, carrots and turnip in big pieces and cook until soft.
Put the leeks in at the end, sliced green and all.
Serve the broth first and the meat after, in the same bowl.
dishes.twist: The receipt is in the family service drawer in his father's hand, and Noel has never cooked from it. He cooks from a typed copy so the original is never touched.
dishes.note: Eaten off the daily plates. The family tureen stands on its chalk mark in the next room, full of nothing.

dishes.name: The Departure Sandwich
method: Spread the deviled ham thick on rye.
Slice the pickle lengthwise and lay it in.
Wrap both sandwiches in waxed paper and string, ready for a train.
Put the tonic and the chocolate in the case with them.
Unwrap them in the lobby at midnight when the car has not come.
dishes.twist: Packed fresh every morning for a departure that keeps not happening. The waxed paper is folded so it can be wrapped again, and it is.
dishes.note: They did not give their names. They gave me the receipt, which I think is more.

dishes.name: Bigos, Built Over a Week
dishes.origin: Poland; Kraków, a house her father drew
method: Soak the mushrooms. Rinse half the sauerkraut and keep half sour.
Fry the bacon and sausage, then the shredded cabbage in their fat.
Layer everything in the big pot with the mushrooms and their water, the prunes, the tomatoes, bay and allspice.
Cook it three hours the first day. Then reheat it every day for a week, adding what is left over.
It is ready when it has been reheated enough to have a history.
dishes.twist: Nadia drafts the week's additions on Quell and Sons letterhead and never signs them. The receipt cards in her drawer are the only drawings she owns with her name left off on purpose.
dishes.note: Built like a building: foundation first, everything on top load-bearing. She posts the memo after midnight and eats a bowl cold at the mail bank.

dishes.name: Spotted Dog, Never the Last Slice
method: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and soda.
Throw in the raisins and caraway.
Pour in the buttermilk and bring it together with one hand, quickly, no kneading.
Shape a round, cut a deep cross in it to let the fairies out, and bake it hot.
Knock on the bottom. It should sound hollow, like a good valve.
dishes.twist: Cal tunes the oven by ear: he listens to the bread's crust tick as it cools through his hearing aid and grades the bake by pitch. A loaf that sings a clean A is a good one.
dishes.note: He eats it down to the heel and wraps the heel. There are eleven heels in the bread crock. None has been thrown away.

dishes.name: Gemista, Arranged
dishes.origin: Smyrna and Chios; her grandmother's island way
method: Cut the tops off the peppers and keep them as lids.
Cook the onion soft in oil, then the rice, half the tomatoes and the mint.
Fill the peppers three-quarters and put their lids on.
Stand them in a pan with potato wedges between them, pour the rest of the tomatoes and oil over, and bake an hour and a half.
Let them cool a little before serving. They are better looked at warm and eaten tepid.
dishes.twist: Iris arranges the pan as a still life before it goes in, and again when it comes out, for an audience that is not there. Omar's lentils sometimes appear in the filling. Neither of them mentions it.
dishes.note: The painting of this dish on the studio wall faces the room. The dish itself she eats facing the window.

dishes.name: Rumbledethumps, Unphotographed
dishes.origin: The Scottish Borders; Uncle Malcolm's mother's
method: Boil the potatoes and mash them with half the butter.
Shred the cabbage and onion and soften them in the rest of the butter.
Beat them into the potato and pepper it.
Pack it into a dish, cover with cheese and bake until the top is brown.
Eat it at once. The cheese does not wait to be photographed.
dishes.twist: Sacha has a contact sheet of this dish from every angle and has never once eaten it hot. Malcolm made it for them on the roof, and they put the camera down long enough to burn their mouth, which is the whole receipt.
dishes.note: They wrote this out for me in pencil and did not date it, which I am told is new.

dishes.name: Three O'Clock Rarebit
dishes.origin: Wales; written down by his father, abandoned by Jonah on page thirty
method: Melt the butter in a small pan and stir in the grated cheese.
Pour in the lager a little at a time, stirring until it is smooth.
Add the mustard and pepper.
Toast the bread on one side, turn it, and pour the cheese on the untoasted side.
Brown it under the grill until it blisters. Finish it. That is the whole point.
dishes.twist: His father's receipt has an ending: serve it hot. Jonah has written forty openings for the story of this dish at the bodega counter and has never once written that line.
dishes.note: He makes enough for two because whoever is at the counter at three is always hungry.
dishes.red_pencil: Serve it hot. There. Finished for you.

dishes.name: Sauerbraten, Certified
dishes.origin: The Rhineland; Kessler's of Stuyvesant Street
method: Boil the vinegar with water, onions, bay, cloves and allspice, cool it, and pour it over the beef in a crock.
Keep it on ice four days, turning it each morning.
Dry the meat, brown it hard in the lard, and braise it in its marinade for three hours.
Crumble the gingersnaps into the strained gravy until it thickens and turns sweet-sour.
Slice it across the grain and serve it with a pickle. Kessler's, naturally.
dishes.twist: Kessler's pickles are her uncle's firm, and the four-day marinade is timed by the iceman's knock, which she has recorded and catalogued. The Estate ledger in her bottom shelf may hold the original receipt. She has not checked.
dishes.note: She is certain of every step. She has never once tasted it as a child would remember it, and has decided not to mind.
dishes.red_pencil: Open the ledger. It may say something different.
